name: PostHog
desc: Funnels, session replay, feature flags and experiments in one tool, self-hostable. Use when you want product analytics without wiring four vendors.

name: Mixpanel
desc: Event analytics with cohorts and retention reports. Use when product managers live inside funnel analysis.

name: Amplitude
desc: Behavioural analytics with strong cohort and journey tooling. Use for large consumer products with dedicated analysts.

name: Google Analytics
desc: Free traffic analytics tied to Google Ads. Use when marketing needs attribution and campaign reporting.

name: Plausible
desc: Cookie-free lightweight analytics, self-hostable. Use when you want visitor numbers without a consent banner.

name: Umami
desc: Open-source privacy-first web analytics on your own database. Use for a free self-hosted Plausible.

name: Matomo
desc: Full-featured analytics you host, with raw data ownership. Use where GDPR makes Google Analytics awkward.

name: Power BI
desc: Microsoft BI with DAX models and Office integration. Use where the business already runs on Excel and Azure.

name: Tableau
desc: Exploratory visual analysis for analysts. Use when discovery and storytelling matter more than embedding.

name: Looker
desc: Governed metrics defined once in LookML. Use when every team must agree on what revenue means.

name: Metabase
desc: Self-hosted BI that non-technical users can actually query. Use to give the team dashboards this week.

name: Apache Superset
desc: Open-source exploration and dashboarding over SQL sources. Use when licences are out and Python is in.

name: Recharts
desc: Composable React chart components over D3. Use for standard dashboards where sensible defaults beat total control.

name: Chart.js
desc: Canvas charts with almost no setup. Use for a handful of charts on a plain page.

name: D3.js
desc: Low-level data-driven DOM manipulation. Use when the visualisation does not exist in any chart library.

name: Apache ECharts
desc: Large chart catalogue that stays fast with huge datasets. Use for dense analytical dashboards.

name: Plotly
desc: Interactive scientific charts with a Python API. Use in notebooks and data apps.

name: visx
desc: D3 primitives as React components, no chart opinions. Use when the design is bespoke but you want React rendering.

name: Segment
desc: Collects events once and fans them out to every tool. Use when marketing keeps asking for another tracking script.

name: RudderStack
desc: Warehouse-first customer data pipeline, self-hostable. Use when event data must land in your warehouse first.
